sections.content:
The course can become highly challenging as it progresses, especially for absolute beginners in coding.

- operators, data types, string operations

sections.teaching: Understanding that the material can be difficult for students, the professor guides the class at a steady pace, covering numerous examples and interactive problem-solving sessions. Consequently, paying close attention during lectures is key to achieving a high grade
sections.grading:
in-class ex 10%
assignment 20%
final exam 70%

The final exam consists of only three extended questions in Part 2, focusing on functions and control structures, and two long questions in Part 3 covering Streamlit and web scraping. Beginners  can easily navigate this because the test is completely open-book, allowing you to bring up to 30 reference sheets into the room. With this setup, you will have plenty of leeway to look up the necessary slides during the exam.

Professor Wang's review sessions are genuinely helpful. The actual test mirrored the practice paper closely. Her lecture carries numerous sample problems and coding alongside students.

From my experience, I didn't even start cramming until the final break, yet I walked away with a B+. Considering my assignment scores weren't even flawless, I found her assessment criteria to be remarkably lenient. The key to doing well is mastering the instructor's in-class demonstrations and practicing their variations. When it comes to the Streamlit portion specifically, staying engaged during lectures and revising your past tasks will be more than enough to succeed.
sections.workload: The course has a low workload with minimal assignments and only one exam, making it completely manageable if you prepare in advance; however, since it is easy to miss minor details in the assignments, I highly recommend double-checking your work with an AI before submission

On the other hand, I do wish the requirements for the individual project could be clearer, which could have saved me time in trying to figure out what kind of program’s required.
The group project is on Selenium and the workload is quite light.
All in all, I would say the workload is not that horrible.  As long as you have put in the effort to study for the three in class exercises, you are good to go for the other components as well.
